title: Retail loan book: early delinquency review

findings.headline: Early delinquency has nearly doubled since Q2 2025
findings.detail: The 30-days-past-due rate at 6 months rose from 6.6% in Q2 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, against 8.8% overall (440 of 5,000 loans). Volumes were flat at about 1,000 loans a quarter, so this is not a mix-of-volume effect.

findings.headline: Deterioration is concentrated in Personal and Card loans
findings.detail: Personal rose from 9.3% to 21.0% and Card from 11.2% to 20.2% between Q1 25 and Q1 26. Car stayed near 6% and Home stayed at or below 1.1%.

findings.headline: Shared phone numbers go with very high delinquency
findings.detail: Nine phone values repeat across 42 loans, and 83.3% of those loans reached 30+ days past due. 81% missed their first payment, against 2.3% across the whole book, which is a possible fraud signal.

findings.headline: Digital and self-employed borrowers show higher delinquency
findings.detail: Digital is at 13.0% against 5.8% for Branch, and Digital's average bureau score is lower (715.4 against 733.7). Self-employed is at 12.2% against 6.5% for Salaried. These groups may overlap with Personal and Card, which this summary cannot separate.

findings.headline: Income is missing mainly for Partner-channel loans
findings.detail: Income is missing for 6.9% of loans, and 90.8% of those gaps are Partner loans (39.7% of Partner loans). Any income-based analysis will under-represent this channel.

next_steps: Investigate the 42 loans sharing phone numbers: check application details, linked accounts and who sourced them, and consider holding similar new applications.
Check whether Q1 26 loans have a full 6-month history, then review Personal and Card underwriting and approvals since Q3 25.
Break delinquency down by product, channel and employment together, and ask the Partner channel to supply missing income data.

conclusion: Early delinquency is rising, from 6.6% in Q2 25 to 12.8% in Q1 26, and the rise sits almost entirely in Personal and Card loans. First, check that the Q1 26 figure is based on full 6-month histories, then review Personal and Card lending since Q3 25. The shared-phone group is a smaller but striking pattern that also needs a look.
limits: This review uses summary statistics only, so it cannot show causes, overlaps between product, channel and employment, or whether recent loans have had a full 6 months to show delinquency.
